name: How do contractors make a drywall patch match the surrounding wall texture?

mainEntity.name: How do contractors make a drywall patch match the surrounding wall texture?

acceptedAnswer.text: Seamless texture matching requires applying the proper technique—such as orange peel, knockdown, or smooth finish—to replicate the existing wall before priming. Drywall mud shrinks as it dries, so a contractor builds thin layers, feathering compound several inches past the damaged zone. Once cured, texture is applied using a hopper, sponge, or spray rig to match the surrounding wall density. If texture is skipped, the repair will reflect light differently than the rest of the wall, making the patch noticeable even under fresh paint.
acceptedAnswer.description: Contractors feather joint compound past the repair edges, sand it flat, and apply matching texture—like orange peel or knockdown—so light reflects evenly across the repaired wall.
